meta.themeSetting: per-account: Dashboard > Your account > Settings > UI THEME (Penpot Dark (default) | Penpot Light | System theme); applies live to open workspace tabs, no reload needed
meta.note: Schema authored fresh by panel-designer for this run -- the architect's original schema (referenced from STATE.md panel-20) was never persisted anywhere this execution could read. This file is now the canonical source of truth; 02-measurements.md is generated from it.

measuredRowOriginsYPxDarkTheme.note: absolute page Y at 100% zoom, viewport top-anchored; illustrates the 4px/16px alternating rhythm, not an api contract

nudgeLadder.supersedes: the ±8 value tried and abandoned on origin/fix/inspector-field-ergonomics -- that was a guess, this is measured. The real value matches what that branch called 'Figma's model' (Shift=±10).

scrub.dragHandle: the field's own 16x16 icon-label glyph (e.g. the character-x icon left of the X axis input), not a separate strip or the label text
scrub.note: shiftRatioPxPerUnit expressed as unit-per-px inverse would be 10 units per 1px; kept as measured: a 100px shift-drag moved the value by 1000, a 100px unmodified drag moved it by 100

tabOrderFromWidthField: (Fill section controls follow in reading order)

keyboardBehavior.enter: commits the field and blurs it
keyboardBehavior.escape: does NOT revert. Measured: focused the X axis field (value 100), selected all text, typed 500, pressed Escape -- field blurred with value permanently set to 500, shape moved on canvas. Treat any 'Esc reverts' assumption in Studio's own inspector as unverified against Penpot and worth re-checking on its own merits, not inherited from this baseline.
keyboardBehavior.arithmeticInFields: supported inline -- typing '100+50' into a numeric field and pressing Enter commits 150

duplicateShortcut.note: the raw keyboard shortcut did not reliably reach the app under browser automation; the context-menu entry is authoritative and is what building the F1 mixed-value sub-case used

designTab.numericField: the literal text 'Mixed' replaces the value (e.g. the X field shows the word Mixed instead of a number, still inside the normal field chrome)
designTab.fillSection: collapses to a single row reading the text 'Mixed' in place of a swatch+hex+opacity row, with only a remove ('-') button retained
designTab.strokeSection: if the property is NOT mixed across the selection (e.g. both shapes share the same stroke), it renders normally -- Mixed is per-property, not per-selection
designTab.selectedColorsSection: a section separate from Fill/Stroke that lists EVERY distinct color used anywhere in the selection, each as its own full swatch+hex+opacity row plus a 'select items using this style' icon that re-selects just the shapes using that color

inspectTab.header: shows '<N> Selected' (e.g. '2 Selected') instead of a layer name
inspectTab.perPropertyRendering: does NOT use the word Mixed -- repeats the property's label as its own row once per distinct value (e.g. two separate 'Background' rows, one per fill color, each with its own swatch+hex+opacity)
inspectTab.geometrySection: the 'Size and position' section is omitted entirely (not shown with Mixed placeholders) when values would be mixed across the selection

inlineRowComposition: swatch (click target for the full picker)
colorFieldChrome.fullPickerPopover: not captured -- clicking the swatch under synthetic pointer automation did not reliably open the saturation/hue popover; not blocking since the inline row above is what the large majority of edits use

addPropertyConvention.emptySectionRender: Title + trailing '+' button, one 32px row, no chevron
addPropertyConvention.onAddClick: reveals the section's fields AND writes a real default value immediately (e.g. clicking Stroke's '+' writes a visible 1px solid black stroke, not a zero/placeholder value)
addPropertyConvention.contrastWithStudio: Studio's own AddablePropertyField (docs/features/inspector-disclosure.md Law 3) explicitly reveals a row and writes NOTHING until the user commits a value -- this is a deliberate, already-decided difference (Studio edits real source files; a silent default write would be a surprising diff), not a gap to close

steps: type into the Fill hex field
click Stroke's '+' (writes a real default stroke on click, no further input needed for a visible result)
type into the Font Size field
type into the column-gap field (row-gap is disabled in single-row mode)
select the image, switch to Inspect tab
